SMTO-DB-0015 — The database server's port number isn't valid

GUID: 1478627a-c969-4b4e-8d6b-5909b3edd694
Slug: database-discovery-port-invalid
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to find the databases on a server, but the port, the number that tells SMTO which door on the server to use, was missing or not a valid number. SMTO didn't connect to anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Enter the port as a number only, with no letters or spaces. PostgreSQL usually uses 5432. SMTO only accepts whole numbers from 1 to 65535 here.
  2. If 5432 doesn't work later, ask the person who manages the database which port it uses. Some servers are set up on a different port, and only the right one will connect.
  3. Send the request again. Nothing was attempted the first time, so it's safe to send again once the port is valid.

What success looks like

  • The search connects to the server and lists the databases it found as drafts you can review.

If it still fails

  • Ask the person who manages the database to confirm its port. If you share the request for help, leave out the password.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A database discovery request's port could not be converted to an integer, or the value is outside 1 through 65535 (invalid_port), so no connection was attempted.

What this means

  • Discovery cannot convert its port to an integer, or the resulting value is outside 1 through 65535. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • Discovery cannot convert its port to an integer, or the resulting value is outside 1 through 65535.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the supplied port with the actual intended listener; this validation makes no network connection.

How to fix it

  • Set port to the PostgreSQL listener's integer port between 1 and 65535 (PostgreSQL's default is 5432). Confirm the actual value with the database administrator or the server's postgresql.conf rather than guessing.
  • Set the actual PostgreSQL listener port in the discovery request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid listener port passes discovery request validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
